date_note: 1Password's post of 25 November discloses the incident; it says it began investigating on 19 November. The page gives no earlier disclosure day.
geo_basis: headquarters city (Toronto) is not stated on the pages read; pin is a general location for the company, not the victim's city
title: 1Password says an attacker used an employee's GitHub account to reach backend systems and download account records for a subset of users; vaults not affected
summary: 1Password says it began investigating unauthorized access on 19 November. According to its post, an attacker used an employee's corporate GitHub account to reach source code and the CI/CD system and push malicious code to backend services, which downloaded account records for "a subset of our users", including names and email addresses. 1Password says customer vaults were not affected.
plain: 1Password says an attacker got into backend systems through an employee's GitHub account and took account records, such as names and email addresses, for some users. It says vault contents were not affected.
exec: 1Password says an attacker reached its backend via an employee's GitHub account and copied account records for a subset of users; it says vaults were not affected.
action: 1Password advises that users do not need to update anything in their account and to be wary of unexpected emails, texts or calls about 1Password; it says it will never ask for your account password or Secret Key.

sources.name: 1Password: Update on a security incident involving 1Password's backend systems

validation.note: 1Password's own post is the primary source; ITmedia Enterprise (Japan) independently relays it.
